articles.body:

articles.title: Gamer react as New Zealand first to see Grand Theft Auto 6
articles.summary: The new game has now been launched in New Zealand with countries around the world set to be able to download it from midnight local time.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has now officially been released in New Zealand and players have had the chance to take their first look at the game.

POPE NZL and Hayden 'Prawln' Tresch, both New Zealand streamers and among the first to download the newest version in the series, praised its soundtrack and graphics.

It will now launch in successive countries at midnight local time with those who had preinstalled it able from then to download it to their consoles.

Its launch had been delayed twice and comes 13 years after GTA V.

articles.body: While it sometimes feels like a chore, regularly cleaning your home can be rewarding. The satisfaction of sparkling dishes, a spotless sink and freshly laundered clothes can reduce stress and give you more time to focus on things you enjoy, like being outdoors, gardening or traveling. It’s very effective and it does a great job of holding onto dust particles without them flying all over. It’s perfect for cleaning pet messes from carpets and upholstered furniture as well as stains from spilled food and beverages. It separates clean and dirty water as it cleans and it comes with a bottle of cleaning solution and a brush attachment to make cleaning messes easier. Some areas of the home are easier to clean than others, and some spots we simply forget to clean. This under-appliance microfiber duster comes recommended by Rodriguez, who says it’s the perfect size for cleaning these spaces. “It’s slim and the long handle makes it easy to reach those tight spaces underneath appliances and furniture,” she says. You can use the device to clean under couches, ovens, refrigerators and even between appliances that are close together. If you save cleaning your shower for last, this squeegee may make you switch up your routine. This stainless steel squeegee helps you clean glass doors, mirrors, windows and tiles of your bathroom, preventing water stains. It comes with a holder that attaches to tiles or glass, which also helps it dry in between washes. Also, it works great for cleaning windows on your car. Every cleaning routine should have at least one handheld appliance to help clean carpets, upholstery and more. The Shark StainForce has the power of a vacuum but the cleaning abilities of a stain removing cleaning solution. As much as we love the original Scrub Daddy, we could wax poetic about the Scrub Mommy multi-surface cleaning sponge too. It’s dual-sided — one is a sponge and the other a dish scrubber. When you soak it in warm water, the sponge becomes soft and when soaked in cold water, it firms up. This fun, eco-friendly tool lets you clean your microwave without scrubbing. Just fill Mama's head with vinegar and water, then microwave her for seven minutes and let the steam rise and do its thing. The steam softens any messes and stains, and once Mama cools down, you can use the leftover liquid inside her to wipe the microwave clean, according to the brand. It even says you can add a squeeze of lemon juice for a clean citrus smell. Angry Mama is dishwasher-safe and made with heat-resistant, nontoxic materials. If your fridge has an odor that never seems to go away, consider this reusable deodorizer from Fringe Ninja. Besides prolonging the freshness of your food, it also comes with a fridge thermometer to help you gauge if the environment is too warm or cold, according to the brand. Reviewers say they like how the charcoal deodorizer works fast and doesn’t take up too much space. Cleaning up after pets that shed a lot can be challenging. Plus, one of these dryer sheets is nearly three times the size of a typical one, so you don’t have to use as many sheets each time you do laundry. This duster brush helps turn dirty blinds clean. It’s designed to clean vents and air conditioners too. The kit also comes with an extender attachment to help clean tight spaces and hard-to-reach areas such as stove grates, drip pans and your car’s crevices. It’s made of 100% recyclable materials and you can use it over and over again — just open the outer shell, rinse off the inner ball with water and snap it together. This mini desktop vacuum cleaner suctions up crumbs, seeds and dust from hard-to-reach places like a computer keyboard. Despite it being a vacuum, it’s not loud, says former NBC Select senior editor Lindsay Schneider. Its batteries last about 2.5 hours, and it has a 360-degree rotatable design so you can wheel it around in all directions, according to the brand. There is an attached brush under the vacuum to swipe away stubborn crumbs. It also comes in a rechargeable version. This list wouldn’t be complete without Mr. Clean’s Magic Eraser, which Zahoransky calls “a must for every household.” The Magic Eraser can tackle a wide variety of seemingly impossible-to-clean messes including removing wall marks and silver tarnish — all with just water, according to the brand. When it comes to laundry, washing and drying is only part of the task. It’s important to also make sure your clothes are free of any lint or piling. This fabric shaver from Beautural is a good solution for apparel that could use some sprucing up. The device removes lint, dust and fuzz from upholstery, blankets, sweaters and jerseys, according to the brand. Another laundry essential, this folding board is a great way to make putting away clothes quicker and easier. You can place the board on a flat surface and fold t-shirts and pants with almost zero effort. A reliable spin mop and bucket are a must for regularly cleaning around the home. This popular item is equipped with a built-in mechanism for wringing out excess water from the microfiber mop head that you operate with your foot. Plus, the mop head itself is machine washable and reusable, but you can also easily replace it every so often, according to the brand. Use the device on hardwood floors, laminate and tile. How I picked the best Amazon cleaning gadgets To compile a list of the best Amazon cleaning gadgets, I chose items with a rating of at least four stars, and whose reviews mention durability and ease of use as reasons shoppers love them. Some of our picks also come recommended by NBC Selected staff, and Rodriguez and Zahoransky. How often should you clean your house? You should thoroughly clean your kitchen and bathrooms, dust all the surfaces in your home and vacuum and clean all hardwood once a week,” says Zahoransky. Additionally, you should keep in mind commonly forgotten areas, such as ceiling fans, baseboards, air vents and window tracks, according to Rodriguez. Sprays such as Method all-purpose cleaner, Mrs. Meyer’s multi-surface everyday cleaner and Seventh Generation disinfecting multi-surface cleaner are all good options for cleaning more common surfaces such as in the kitchen or bathroom, says Rodriguez. articles.body:
Mada Masr’s Lina Attalah due to appear before court in Egypt

Mada Masr Editor-in-Chief Lina Attalah is set to face a retrial before an Egyptian criminal court on Wednesday, after being sentenced in absentia to one year in prison for operating an unlicensed website and spreading ‘false news’. The court has also ordered the closure of the independent news outlet.

articles.title: Natal Solidário em Campo Grande: Campanha ajuda 226 crianças | G1
articles.standfirst: Campanha da Associação Lar do Pequeno Assis pretende arrecadar R$ 22,6 mil com doações de R$ 100 por criança. Evento será realizado em 16 de dezembro, no bairro Tiradentes.
articles.summary: O Natal Solidário em Campo Grande arrecada doações para a ceia de 226 crianças do Lar do Pequeno Assis; contribua com R$ 100 e ajude famílias do bairro Tiradentes.
articles.body:
Jovens que fazem parte da ong em Campo Grande — Foto: Arquivo ALPA

A campanha “Adote uma Criança”, da Associação Lar do Pequeno Assis (ALPA), busca arrecadar R$ 22,6 mil para garantir a ceia de Natal de 226 crianças e seus familiares em Campo Grande .

A iniciativa propõe doações de R$ 100, valor destinado a custear a refeição de cada criança e de seus familiares. O Natal Solidário será realizado em 16 de dezembro, às 19h, na sede da instituição, no bairro Tiradentes.

A expectativa é reunir cerca de 500 pessoas, entre crianças atendidas pelos projetos sociais, pais e irmãos. A programação inclui jantar, bebidas e sobremesa. A instituição também recebe brinquedos novos para entregar às crianças durante o evento.

A adoção é simbólica e pode ser feita por pessoas físicas, empresas e voluntários. Cada doação de R$ 100 ajuda a custear a ceia de uma criança e de seus familiares.

Informações para realizar a doação: WhatsApp (67) 98165-5171

A meta é arrecadar o valor correspondente a 226 cotas de adoção simbólica, uma para cada criança atendida pela instituição.

Crianças durante atividades oferecidas pelo ONG. — Foto: Arquivo ALPA

Localizada no bairro Tiradentes, a Associação Lar do Pequeno Assis atende 226 crianças em situação de vulnerabilidade social. A instituição oferece atividades no contraturno escolar, com ações esportivas, culturais e de fortalecimento de vínculos.

Entre as atividades estão ginástica artística, judô, handebol, xadrez, artes, fotografia, dança e música. Em 2026, a associação completa 20 anos de atuação.

*Estagiária sob supervisão de José Câmara.

articles.title: Operação investiga indução de jovens à automutilação em SC e SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Três mandados de busca e apreensão foram cumpridos nos municípios de São Francisco do Sul (SC) e na capital paulista. Duas adolescentes são suspeitas de aliciar outros jovens.
articles.summary: Operação contra automutilação em redes sociais cumpre mandados em SC e SP após descoberta de grupo que usava manipulação psicológica para aliciar jovens.
articles.body:
Jovem em frente a tela de computador — Foto: Sofia Mayer/g1

Um grupo nas redes sociais suspeito de induzir adolescentes à automutilação é alvo de uma operação em Santa Catarina e no estado de São Paulo . Segundo o Ministério Público catarinense (MPSC), três mandados de busca e apreensão foram cumpridos em São Francisco do Sul (SC) e na capital paulista na manhã desta quarta-feira (18).

Duas adolescentes são investigadas por aliciar outros jovens e coagir as vítimas a praticarem atos abusivos e de autolesão. Conforme a investigação, isso era feito a partir de manipulação psicológica, intimidação e controle emocional.

Durante os cumprimentos dos mandados pelo Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate às Organizações Criminosas (Gaeco), foram apreendidos dispositivos eletrônicos e equipamentos de informática, que passarão por perícia e análise para aprofundar as investigações.

A investigação foi aberta após a descoberta da existência de grupos em redes sociais supostamente utilizados para essas práticas. O objetivo da ação é identificar possíveis vítimas e outros envolvidos, além de subsidiar ações de proteção e resgate de adolescentes.

As investigações continuam e estão sob sigilo.

Um asfalto cedeu após um vazamento de água e "engoliu" um caminhão betoneira na manhã desta quarta-feira (18), no bairro Vivendas II, em Votuporanga (SP).

articles.title: Nvidia descarta volta de Jensen Huang ao comando da empresa e promete acelerar busca por novo CEO | G1
articles.standfirst: Saída de Huang ocorreu em meio a um escândalo envolvendo casos extraconjugais e suspeitas de espionagem chinesa. Apesar da crise, a Nvidia divulgou projeções de receita acima das expectativas do mercado.
articles.summary: Saída de Huang ocorreu em meio a um escândalo envolvendo casos extraconjugais e suspeitas de espionagem chinesa.
articles.body:
O presidente do conselho da Nvidia , Harvey Jones, abriu uma teleconferência com investidores na terça-feira (18) afirmando que a empresa não recontrataria o cofundador Jensen Huang como presidente-executivo nem responderia a perguntas sobre sua saída.

Somadas aos sólidos resultados da companhia, as declarações de Jones foram uma resposta contundente ao movimento que defende a volta de Huang, que deixou o cargo na semana passada .

Com a saída de Huang, os investidores buscam pistas sobre o futuro e a estratégia da Nvidia , desde seus compromissos bilionários com provedores de nuvem, fornecedores e startups de IA até quem liderará, em última instância, a fabricante de chips mais valiosa do mundo.

Jones disse que o conselho contratou a empresa de recrutamento executivo Heidrick & Struggles para ajudar na busca por um novo presidente-executivo.

“Queremos nomear o presidente-executivo, o presidente-executivo permanente, o mais rápido possível, mas não vamos apressar a nomeação antes de encontrar exatamente a pessoa certa”, acrescentou.

Na teleconferência, Jones foi acompanhado pela CEO interina Colette Kress, que também é diretora financeira, e pelo engenheiro Ian Buck, vice-presidente de computação em hiperescala e alto desempenho.

“Ter a combinação de Kress, Jones e Buck na teleconferência foi uma jogada inteligente, pois garantiu que eles estivessem preparados para lidar com questões financeiras, técnicas e estratégicas de alto nível. Além disso, foi um passo necessário para mostrar ao mundo uma gama mais ampla de vozes de dentro da Nvidia ”, disse Bob O’Donnell, analista-chefe da TECHnalysis Research.

As ações da empresa subiam 4% no pregão após o fechamento, depois que a Nvidia divulgou uma previsão de vendas acima das estimativas de Wall Street.

Ainda assim, o valor de mercado da empresa, de US$ 3,8 trilhões , está cerca de US$ 2 trilhões abaixo da máxima registrada no início de outubro.

Kress defendeu o trabalho da equipe desde a saída de Huang. “Nossa liderança se mostrou muito forte na última semana”, disse ela. “Estamos no controle.”

A liderança da Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co, que fabrica chips para a Nvidia , estava no escritório e “totalmente empenhada em nos ajudar”, afirmou ela.

Em declarações preparadas, Kress acrescentou que o mais recente chip emblemático de IA da empresa, chamado Vera Rubin, teve um início explosivo.

As ações de provedores especializados em nuvem para IA — CoreWeave, Nebius, IREN e Applied Digital — ampliaram os ganhos depois que Kress disse aos analistas que, embora a fabricante de chips imponha condições aos seus investimentos, não fez mudanças na forma como cumpre seus compromissos com a “neocloud”.

Huang, amplamente visto como o rosto público do boom da IA, renunciou na quinta-feira após revelações de casos extraconjugais, incluindo um com a empresária chinesa Alice Huang e dois com funcionárias da Nvidia .

Agências de inteligência dos EUA tentam determinar a extensão dos laços de Alice Huang com o Ministério de Segurança do Estado da China e quais informações ela pode ter repassado a Pequim, segundo duas fontes a par do assunto.

A China rejeitou as alegações de uma operação de espionagem com Jensen Huang como alvo. A Comissão de Valores Mobiliários dos EUA (SEC) está investigando a Nvidia após a renúncia de Huang ao cargo de presidente-executivo na semana passada, informou o Wall Street Journal na tarde de terça-feira. A SEC se recusou a comentar.

A saída de Huang encerrou três décadas de liderança direta do fundador sobre o desenvolvimento de chips da Nvidia , os acordos com clientes e os laços com Washington, tornando a execução um risco maior do que a demanda por IA no curto prazo, segundo analistas.

A ausência de Huang, um presidente-executivo conhecido pelo perfil extrovertido, também contribuiu para uma teleconferência de resultados bem mais curta, encerrada em menos de uma hora.

“Não é surpresa que eles estejam indo muito bem, e haverá pessoas que darão um suspiro de alívio com isso”, disse Rick Meckler, sócio da Cherry Lane Investments. “Mas a história aqui é muito complicada, e é difícil não levar isso em conta como um risco adicional para quem está comprando ações.”

Perspectivas para o quarto trimestre superam expectativas

A empresa espera receita de US$ 130 bilhões (cerca de R$ 753,9 bilhões) no quarto trimestre, com variação de mais ou menos 3%, acima da estimativa média dos analistas, de US$ 125,25 bilhões (cerca de R$ 726,4 bilhões) , segundo dados da LSEG. A Nvidia informou que a projeção não leva em conta vendas de chips para data centers na China.

A margem bruta ajustada deve ficar entre 71% e 72%, ante a estimativa dos analistas de 71,7%.

Anshel Sag, analista principal da Moor Insights & Strategy, disse que as perspectivas da Nvidia são “bastante positivas, embora não tão ambiciosas quanto nos trimestres anteriores, o que muitos já haviam previsto”.

Ele acrescentou: “Não acho que nada no curto prazo será afetado pela saída de Jensen. Sua equipe de liderança executiva é competente e, ao longo dos anos, seguiu sua liderança e atuou de forma eficaz, chegando a este ponto.”

O conselho considera candidatos internos e externos para o cargo de presidente-executivo, e Kress é vista como capaz de oferecer liderança estável durante o processo de seleção.

Mas o processo de escolha ficou mais complicado com o crescimento de uma campanha chamada “Stand With Jensen” (“Apoie Jensen”), que defende sua permanência.

Na terça-feira, Huang afirmou que ficaria “honrado” em voltar ao cargo, caso o conselho da empresa considerasse essa a melhor decisão.

Thomas Markle, pai da duquesa de Sussex, em entrevista à emissora britânica ITV — Foto: Good Morning Britain/ITV handout via Reuters

Um promotor regional das Filipinas afirmou nesta quarta-feira (18) à agência AFP que a polícia pediu o indiciamento de Thomas Markle, pai de Meghan Markle, por suspeita de posse e distribuição de material de abuso sexual infantil.

O inquérito policial foi apresentado na segunda-feira (16), na província de Cebu, onde as autoridades acreditam que Thomas tenha vivido durante um ano. A informação foi confirmada pelo promotor Graeme Elmido à AFP.

A polícia recomenda que Markle responda a duas acusações de distribuição de pornografia infantil e a uma de posse desse tipo de material.

"As denúncias serão submetidas a uma avaliação preliminar e, se as provas justificarem, Thomas Markle será intimado a responder às acusações no âmbito da investigação", afirmou Elmido.

Thomas Markle, pai da duquesa de Sussex, em entrevista à emissora britânica ITV; e Meghan Markle chega para visita a universidade em Johannesburgo, na África do Sul — Foto: Good Morning Britain/ITV handout via Reuters e Michele Spatari / AFP

Thomas Markle, de 82 anos, também é investigado nos Estados Unidos. Ele foi detido por agentes do FBI na casa de repouso onde vivia, na Flórida, sob suspeita de posse de material de abuso sexual infantil. A juíza responsável pelo caso solicitou uma avaliação psiquiátrica do investigado.

Além dos Estados Unidos e das Filipinas, há uma investigação em andamento no México, onde autoridades revistaram um depósito supostamente alugado por Markle.

No início de novembro, a polícia filipina informou ter encontrado material de abuso sexual infantil em três cartões de memória e em um telefone celular apreendidos em uma suposta antiga residência de Thomas Markle.

O ministro do Interior das Filipinas, Jonvic Remulla, disse à AFP que o país adotaria "as medidas legais correspondentes" caso fossem encontradas provas suficientes.

Thomas Markle nega todas as acusações. Ele está afastado da filha, Meghan, desde o casamento dela com o príncipe Harry, em 2018.

articles.title: Trump, Putin e Xi: Reunião em Shenzhen marca nova era diplomática | G1
articles.standfirst: Reunião inédita entre três líderes autoritários reforça a posição do presidente russo no cenário internacional e amplia o protagonismo da China.
articles.summary: O encontro inédito entre Trump, Putin e Xi Jinping na China foca no simbolismo do G-3 e pode alterar os rumos das guerras na Ucrânia e no Irã sob a mediação de Pequim.
articles.body:
Há mais simbolismo do que expectativa de resultados ambiciosos na poderosa imagem que será produzida durante a reunião de três líderes autoritários nesta quinta-feira (18) em Shenzhen, no sul da China .

Donald Trump , Xi Jinping e Vladimir Putin se preparam para ensaiar a coreografia do encontro que, apelidado de G-3, serve mais aos interesses dos três e ofusca a cúpula da Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico (APEC).

Visto como pária pelo Ocidente, ele retorna ao xadrez diplomático em grande estilo, aparentemente em pé de igualdade com os líderes de duas superpotências . Esta equivalência já faz dele um vencedor.

Embora a pauta do encontro seja vaga e a guerra da Rússia na Ucrânia tenha ficado de fora da agenda, é difícil imaginar que o conflito não seja abordado. Com pouca disposição para encerrar a guerra, Putin deve tentar angariar o apoio de Xi para levar Trump a pressionar ainda mais o governo ucraniano.

“Putin tem todos os motivos para sorrir ao se dirigir para a reunião trilateral. No momento, Putin e inúmeros analistas russos acreditam que ele transformou o governo Trump em um facilitador de fato do esforço de guerra de Moscou”, pondera o diretor do Centro Eurásia do think tank Atlantic Council, John Herbst.

Os presidentes da Rússia, Vladimir Putin, da China, Xi Jinping, e dos EUA, Donald Trump — Foto: Reuters

O pesquisador assinala como exemplos desta influência a assinatura do acordo com a Rússia para exportar mais combustível diesel , a suspensão das sanções - prevista no projeto de lei de Lindsey Graham - o corte das operações dos satélites Starlink e Starshield em Kiev e a concordância com a proposta de Putin de uma reunião trilateral com Xi.

O presidente da China, por sua vez, exercerá com cautela o papel de anfitrião, em busca de obter mais influência na diplomacia global.

O país vem fornecendo à Rússia apoio econômico e político, mas evita respaldar abertamente o Kremlin na guerra que se desenrola há quase cinco anos. Além disso, a China procura se manter afastada das negociações para pôr fim aos conflitos na Ucrânia e no Irã .

“Xi Jinping se beneficiará do papel de articulador e definidor da agenda das relações entre China, Rússia e Estados Unidos . O encontro destacará a habilidade diplomática de Xi e a centralidade da China no sistema internacional”, avalia Ryan Hass, diretor do Centro John L. Thornton para a China, do Brookings Institution.

Dos três, o presidente americano parece estar em desvantagem ao desembarcar em Shenzhen tentando recuperar o prestígio , seriamente abalado pela rejeição popular nas eleições de meio de mandato , pelo escândalo envolvendo o aliado Jensen Huang , ex-CEO da Nvidia, e pela indefinição sobre um acordo que ponha fim ao conflito o Irã .

Vale lembrar que Trump está em lado oposto ao de Xi e Putin em relação à guerra contra o Irã, mas vem se aproximando do presidente russo nas negociações para uma solução que encerre a guerra entre Rússia e Ucrânia.

Na chegada, Trump teve uma surpresa positiva: foi recebido no aeroporto por Xi, numa rara deferência do presidente chinês com um líder estrangeiro. Um abraço caloroso selou o reencontro entre os dois.

É o passo inicial da coreografia para a reunião de cúpula trilateral que pode institucionalizar um novo formato nas relações entre EUA, China e Rússia, deixando apreensivos os aliados tradicionais de cada um.

articles.title: Líder em casos de Mpox no Brasil, estado de SP recebe mil doses da vacina contra a doença | G1
articles.standfirst: Estado concentra mais de 37% dos 1.055 casos confirmados no país. Distribuição começa na próxima segunda-feira (23). Apesar do aumento dos casos, infectologistas descartam motivo para pânico.
articles.summary: Estado concentra mais de 37% dos 1.055 casos confirmados no país. Distribuição começa na próxima segunda-feira (23). Apesar do aumento dos casos, infectologistas descartam motivo para pânico.
articles.body:
Brasil autoriza compra de até 20 mil doses de vacina contra mpox — Foto: Adobe Stock

O estado de São Paulo recebeu do Ministério da Saúde uma nova remessa de mil doses da vacina contra a Mpox. Os imunizantes serão distribuídos aos serviços de saúde para atender aos grupos prioritários.

Com 398 casos confirmados, São Paulo passou a liderar o número de registros da doença no Brasil, segundo o balanço mais recente do Ministério da Saúde. O estado concentra mais de 37% dos 1.055 casos confirmados no país.

A distribuição das doses começa na próxima segunda-feira (23), com o envio dos imunizantes aos Grupos de Vigilância Epidemiológica (GVEs) do estado. Os órgãos farão o encaminhamento aos municípios, de acordo com a população elegível e o cenário epidemiológico de cada região.

A capital paulista receberá 600 doses. Segundo o governo estadual, a divisão dos imunizantes não considera necessariamente o número total de habitantes de cada cidade.

A vacinação é destinada a pessoas que vivem com HIV/Aids e têm maior comprometimento do sistema imunológico, usuários da profilaxia pré-exposição ao HIV (PrEP) e profissionais de laboratório com exposição ao vírus. Também podem receber a vacina pessoas que tiveram contato de médio ou alto risco com casos suspeitos ou confirmados da doença, após avaliação dos serviços de saúde.

Quem integra os grupos prioritários deve procurar sua unidade de saúde de referência para receber orientações sobre os critérios de elegibilidade e o encaminhamento para a vacinação, conforme a organização da rede municipal.

O que é a Mpox e como ocorre a transmissão?

A Mpox é causada pelo vírus MPXV e pode provocar lesões na pele em diferentes partes do corpo. Os primeiros sintomas costumam ser semelhantes aos de outras infecções, como febre, dores no corpo, fraqueza, dor de cabeça e aumento dos gânglios (ínguas).

Depois, surgem as lesões características da doença: manchas vermelhas que evoluem para bolhas e crostas, que podem aparecer em diferentes regiões do corpo, inclusive na área genital. Outros sintomas possíveis são dor de garganta, congestão nasal, tosse e dores nas costas.

A transmissão ocorre principalmente pelo contato próximo com lesões na pele, fluidos corporais, sangue ou mucosas de pessoas infectadas. Também pode acontecer pelo compartilhamento de objetos recentemente contaminados, como roupas e toalhas.

O contato sexual é uma das formas de transmissão, mas não é a única, explica Eduardo Medeiros, diretor técnico e infectologista do Hospital São Paulo, da Universidade Federal de São Paulo (Unifesp).

"A questão sexual é muito importante nisso porque, se a lesão está no órgão genital, você entra em contato com a mucosa do seu parceiro, da sua parceira. O resultado disso é que a infecção ocorre com mais facilidade e a transmissão também é muito fácil dessa forma. Mas ela não é exclusiva sexual, isso é muito importante a gente dizer", afirma.

O médico também chama a atenção para a possibilidade de transmissão dentro do ambiente familiar, pelo contato direto com as lesões ou, menos frequentemente, por objetos contaminados.

"Existem muitas vezes contatos familiares, inclusive, que podem desenvolver Mpox até pelo contato direto com as lesões ou mesmo, eventualmente, embora seja mais raro, por roupas e toalhas que entraram em contato com a lesão", complementa.

Apesar do aumento dos casos, infectologistas descartam motivo para pânico, mas reforçam a importância das medidas de prevenção, da vacinação dos grupos indicados e da procura por atendimento médico diante dos primeiros sintomas.

Em 2022, primeiro ano da série histórica apresentada, o Brasil registrou 10.591 casos de Mpox. Em 2023, foram 778; em 2024, 1.989; em 2025, 1.075; e, em 2026, 1.055.

São Paulo também teve o maior número de registros em 2022, com 4.199 casos. Nos anos seguintes, foram 143 em 2023, 1.062 em 2024, 375 em 2025 e 398 em 2026, totalizando 6.177 ocorrências.

No Rio de Janeiro, foram 1.331 casos em 2022, 163 em 2023, 330 em 2024, 121 em 2025 e 391 em 2026. O total no período é de 2.336 registros.

articles.title: In 1994, David McArdle and Jodie swapped addresses at a pool table while on holiday in Kos and wrote to each other monthly for three years before losing touch; two decades later, a birthday text reunited them, and they married
articles.summary: In the summer of 1994, David McArdle was holidaying with his family on the Greek island of Kos.
articles.body: In the summer of 1994, David McArdle was holidaying with his family on the Greek island of Kos. Among the other teenagers at the resort was 15-year-old Jodie, who was there on holiday with her family. They had no reason to notice each other, and yet they did. They sat at the resort’s pool table. They were joined by 10 more kids. Twelve strangers from different families, all with different plans for the week, became a pack. Nothing about it looked like the start of anything. It was just a week, a few games and the usual teenage fizz of people who wouldn’t see each other again.Then, before anyone went home, the group began swapping addresses. Nobody expected it to mean anything. But for David and Jodie, that simple ritual changed everything. They became pen pals but later lost contact. Two decades later, fate brought them together, and they are now married!They became pen palsAfter the holiday ended, most of the group drifted apart. But David and Jodie didn’t. They kept writing to each other. They wrote about their schools, friends and interests. Every month, they sent at least one letter to each other. Letters take their time, and that was part of it. Each one gave the other something to wait for. The letters continued for about three years. Then David moved, and the post stopped arriving. Neither of them had a way to track the other down. Life pulled them in separate directions. David was two years older than Jodie, and each of them built a life that had little to do with a pool table on a Greek island.A text message after two decadesDavid and Jodie moved on with their respective lives. Years went by, and then a message arrived on David’s mum’s phone. It was from Jodie, and it said, ‘Happy birthday from me and the girls.’ David had no idea his mother still had Jodie’s number. When he asked her about it, she didn’t have much of an explanation.‘I couldn’t believe I found her again,’ David told Talk to the Press. ‘I said to my mum, “I didn’t know you had Jodie’s number.”’David didn’t think twice. He replied at once, saying it was David. Fifteen minutes later, Jodie replied. Those moments surely felt longer for him. Jodie, who was working as a teaching assistant at the time, replied that she was so glad to hear from him. ‘It turns out that 15-minute wait for her reply was because she was sobbing her heart out looking at the text. She’d wanted to get in touch, but she thought I was in a relationship, so she didn’t want to ruffle any feathers.’For the next two years, they barely stopped talking on the phone. They spent hours learning about each other’s lives. After all, they had decades of conversations pending! Eventually, they met in person for the first time in 24 years. David drove 300 miles to Cardiff to see Jodie. They were over the moon to finally meet each other. On their first meeting, they spent 12 hours together on the sofa, talking about their lives. He went back two weeks later.David and Jodie knew they had a special connection. They eventually started dating. After three years of courtship, David proposed at the top of the London Eye. The couple married soon after and have settled in Cardiff, where they now live together.Every August, they return to Kos, the place where they first met as teenagers. They stay in the same apartments where they first swapped addresses, and they can still picture the pool table!You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: China’s Xi pitches free trade at APEC amid Trump’s global trade disruptions
articles.summary: The president says Beijing seeks to provide a ‘stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises’.
articles.body:
China’s President Xi Jinping has urged support for “free and open trade”, pitching Beijing as a stable partner – as opposed to President Donald Trump-led Washington – and pledging to stand up to trade protectionism.

Speaking on the sidelines of the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit on Wednesday in Shenzhen, southern China, Xi took aim at rising “unilateralism and protectionism”.

His remarks appeared to be a veiled criticism of Trump’s America First policies, under which the United States has imposed tariffs on both allies and economic rivals.

Xi is due to meet Trump, who is travelling from the Philippines for the APEC leaders’ summit later on Wednesday. Xi and Trump are then due to hold an unprecedented three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

On the sidelines of the APEC summit, Xi told business executives that the Asia Pacific must pursue more open trade and equitable growth to remain stable and dynamic.

Trump’s America First approach of tariff hikes and other moves runs counter to APEC’s aim of eventually forming a Pacific Rim free trade zone.

Washington also limits Chinese access to leading-edge US technology, such as the Nvidia computer chips that help power artificial intelligence (AI).

“We must firmly uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system with the World Trade Organization at its core, support free and open trade and investment, maintain the stability and smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains,” Xi said.

He added that China sought to “provide a more stable, predictable and beneficial environment for global enterprises” and would continue to expand access in its manufacturing and services sectors.

“Starting by lowering tariffs, expanding access, and exploring regulations and management standards, China will conduct deep-seated reform,” Xi said.

“While pursuing its own development, China has shared opportunities with other countries and worked for common development,” he said. “It has steadily brought stability and predictability to world economic growth and international trade and economic cooperation.”

George Chen, partner and chair of digital practice at The Asia Group, told the Associated Press news agency that Xi’s speech highlighted China’s aim to lead global industrial transformation.

“While he didn’t say so explicitly, his message was clear: China wants to be seen as a partner in global technology development, in contrast to Washington’s more restrictive approach,” Chen said, noting that Xi did not mention export controls, Nvidia, or the US directly.

Xi’s message is “likely to resonate with many Global South countries, and reinforces Beijing’s effort to contrast its technology strategy with that of Washington”, Chen added.

articles.title: Epstein’s death more likely homicide than suicide, forensic expert says
articles.summary: An analysis of autopsy records and photos suggests the US sex offender was murdered in 2019, an expert says.
articles.body:
A forensic expert has analysed autopsy records and photos that he believes suggest US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein was murdered rather than died by suicide.

Following a years-long investigation, Michael Freeman, editor-in-chief of the Journal of Forensic and Legal Medicine, told the CBS News broadcaster that he had concluded that Epstein was strangled, most likely from behind, while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges in 2019.

“The injuries that were documented by the medical examiner were not consistent with the suicidal hanging,” Freeman said on Monday.

“If you put it all together, it is most consistent with a homicidal strangulation from behind using a narrow knotted fabric ligature,” he added.

Epstein was found hanging in his cell at the Metropolitan Correctional Center in New York on August 10, 2019. An autopsy concluded that he had taken his own life.

His death has long been the subject of conspiracy theories, with some claiming he was killed over fears he would provide damning evidence linking prominent public figures to cases of sexual abuse, rape and paedophilia.

Security cameras outside Epstein’s cell were not recording on the day of his death. A 2023 Department of Justice report concluded that the facility had longstanding problems with its cameras.

Epstein’s brother, Mark, has called for a new investigation following Freeman’s comments. Freeman argued on Monday that the evidence suggests Epstein was strangled with a ligature, which was then used to suspend his body from a bunk bed.

The New York City Office of Chief Medical Examiner said it “stands by its determination”.

articles.title: Northumberland MP urges council to speed up heating oil payments
articles.summary: About 23,000 households use heating oil in Northumberland and face increasing bills this winter.
articles.body:
An MP has urged a council to speed up the process of heating oil support payments as energy prices soar.

About 23,000 Northumberland homes use oil systems as they are not connected to the mains gas supply.

Labour's North Northumberland MP David Smith said a freedom of information request from 21 September showed just over a third of households who applied for help with heating oil costs had received funding from Northumberland County Council.

However, the Conservative-led local authority said its latest figures showed significantly more applications had now been approved almost two months on.

Energy prices have increased due to ongoing conflicts around the world.

Unlike gas, oil prices are not protected by the Ofgem Energy Price Cap, and households have experienced huge increases in the cost of filling tanks.

Smith said the freedom of information request showed there had been 328 applications for heating oil assistance, but only 112 had been approved with total payments amounting to £36,123.

The council said its figures showed more than 160 applicants and 40 venues had been supported, and there was no backlog for residents seeking support with heating oil, according to the Local Democracy Reporting Service.

"Those not receiving support are applicants who have not been able to demonstrate their household is either vulnerable or struggling to afford heating oil due to a low income," a spokesperson said.

The government provided £5m to the county council through its Crisis and Resilience fund in April, including almost £500,000 to support households struggling with the cost of heating oil.

Bamburgh Conservative councillor Guy Renner-Thompson has a home which uses a heating oil system.

He urged the government to bring in more financial support, saying the council fully expected to spend the entire £498,459 heating oil allocation.

articles.title: Myanmar-linked arsenic pollution prompts clean water scramble in Thailand
articles.summary: Thai authorities race to provide safe water to villagers after arsenic from Myanmar mines contaminates Mekong River.
articles.body:
Thai government authorities have raced to provide clean water for more than 20,000 households in northern Thailand after unsafe levels of arsenic, linked to rare earth mining operations in Myanmar, were found in the water supply.

Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul late on Tuesday ordered government agencies to find alternative water sources and closely monitor tap water quality in the province of Chiang Rai, according to deputy government spokeswoman Lalida Persvivatana.

Tap water supplies to thousands of homes in 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended this month after officials found arsenic levels in the local waterworks to be 30 times over the safe limit.

Government authorities also found arsenic contamination in untreated water from the Sai River, a tributary of the Mekong River, at 25 times the limit for drinking water.

Authorities have deployed two trucks to supply residents with clean drinking water, while the government is also considering alternative river water sources.

Researchers at Naresuan University said last week that chemical analysis and satellite modelling traced much of the arsenic-laden sediment in the Sai River to gold mining operations across the border in Myanmar.

A surge in rare earth mining in rebel-held pockets of Myanmar supplying Chinese processing plants is being blamed for toxic levels of heavy metals in Thai waterways, including the Mekong River.

Myanmar’s longrunning civil war enables unregulated exploitation of natural resources, including rare earth elements used in smartphones, wind turbines and electric vehicles.

Thai Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow raised the issue of what he said was a “dramatic” increase in pollution in the Sai River during a visit last week to Myanmar to meet government officials.

He blamed “wastewater from mining”, adding that it was an “urgent matter that needs urgent attention”.

The Thai government says it has also discussed the issue with Beijing, with researchers saying many of the mining operations in Myanmar are Chinese-run.

There are fears the pollution is being washed far down the Mekong River, a waterway supporting millions of people across several countries.

Thai officials said arsenic had been found in the urine of 17 out of 177 people tested in October in the northeastern province of Nong Khai, on the border with Laos.

articles.title: India-UK ties outride Modi’s ‘decolonisation’ rhetoric
articles.summary: Prince William’s visit highlights growing partnership between New Delhi and London, despite their colonial history.
articles.body:
Delivering a lecture in November 2025, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke of the lingering legacy of British rule that the country suffered for two centuries. Though India gained independence in 1947, it still needed to “decolonise the mind,” he said, laying out a decade-long plan to achieve this goal.

But on Wednesday, almost exactly a year after those comments, Modi will host Prince William and his wife, Catherine, the Princess of Wales, in New Delhi, after they also visited Mumbai — playing street cricket alongside Indian legend Sachin Tendulkar to kick off a three-day visit to India.

The British royals, visiting India for the first time in a decade, are attending the Earthshot Prize ceremony, one of the most prestigious environmental awards in the world, founded by William.

Modi’s conversation with the royals is expected to focus on the deep bonds, past and present, between their nations — a reality that analysts say is more powerful than the rhetoric politicians turn to.

The prime minister’s residence is no longer on Race Course Road: Modi renamed the street Lok Kalyan Marg (Public Welfare Street in Sanskrit). Several landmarks and towns named after British colonial-era figures across the country have been renamed under Modi, as have the country’s British-era criminal and penal codes.

Yet beyond that symbolism, India’s relations with the United Kingdom have blossomed over the decades, just as India’s bureaucracy, legal and political systems still remain rooted in institutions set up by the British.

Under Modi, New Delhi has also pursued increasingly close economic ties with London, culminating in a landmark free trade agreement that came into force in July.

“I don’t see an inherent contradiction. India has been moving away from its colonial legacy while building a relationship with Britain ever since 1947,” academic Jaideep Prabhu told Al Jazeera.

“I believe that a more confident India can reclaim its historical narrative while engaging Britain as an equal. The relationship can acknowledge the past without being defined by it,” Prabhu, professor of business and enterprise at Cambridge University, added.

Economic and strategic interests are at the heart of the growing partnership that has seemingly taken precedence over the countries’ complicated history.

Britain’s search for new trading relationships following Brexit has made India an increasingly important partner, said Kate Sullivan de Estrada, associate professor in international relations of South Asia at the University of Oxford.

“As a post-Brexit UK has honed in on global trade and investment opportunities, pursued defence and technological cooperation, and sought partners to address global challenges such as climate change and health, India has emerged as an increasing priority in almost all areas of UK foreign policy,” de Estrada told Al Jazeera.

Echoing de Estrada, Gulshan Sachdeva, a professor at Jawaharlal Nehru University in New Delhi, said Britain’s post-Brexit ambitions, including its growing focus on the Asia Pacific, have converged with India’s economic and strategic priorities.

“Both are trying to transform their shared colonial legacy into a foundation for positive engagement, particularly through deeper economic integration and diaspora linkages,” he told Al Jazeera.

In July 2025, the relationship reached a notable high when Modi and former British Prime Minister Keir Starmer signed a multibillion-dollar trade agreement, which came into force a year later.

The agreement is expected to increase bilateral trade by £25.5bn ($33bn) annually in the long term, according to British government estimates, by reducing tariffs and removing barriers across a range of industries. Trade between the two countries had already reached nearly £48bn ($63bn) in 2025, reflecting the growing economic stakes for both sides.

Oxford’s de Estrada said the agreement also reflected growing global trade uncertainty, particularly following US President Donald Trump’s tariff policies, which encouraged both countries to diversify their economic relationships.

Beyond trade, India and Britain have also increased cooperation in areas of defence and security, as well as emerging technologies and clean energy.

In October 2025, London and New Delhi signed a $465m deal to supply India’s military with UK-manufactured lightweight multirole missiles built in Northern Ireland.

That same month, India’s Ministry of External Affairs announced that New Delhi and London had agreed to establish centres for connectivity, innovation and artificial intelligence , alongside a critical minerals industry group aimed at strengthening supply chains and advancing green technologies.

But Cambridge’s Prabhu noted the relationship between India and the UK is defined by much more than “ties between governments”, pointing to longstanding cultural, sporting and historical connections, as well as Britain’s large Indian diaspora.

“Britain’s large Indian diaspora is an important bridge between the two societies, while Indian parents continue to invest in a British education for their children. There is also an institutional familiarity, given the similarities in our legal, parliamentary and administrative systems,” he added.

About two million people of Indian origin live in the UK today.

Despite their growing partnership, several disagreements between New Delhi and London continue to flare up from time to time.

“One point of tension is diaspora politics,” Edward Anderson, associate professor at Northumbria University and senior fellow at SOAS, the South Asia Institute, told Al Jazeera.

“India sees its diaspora as a potential ally and asset – the huge rallies Modi has held in New York, London and elsewhere clearly illustrate that. But India simultaneously sees the diaspora as a possible threat and liability.”

One of the most contentious issues involves the Khalistan movement , which seeks the creation of an independent Sikh homeland in India’s Punjab region.

Britain is home to a large Sikh diaspora, including supporters of the separatist movement, whose activities have repeatedly drawn criticism from Indian officials.

New Delhi views Khalistani separatism as a threat to its territorial integrity and has accused British authorities of failing to adequately address the activities of groups it considers extremist.

The issue came to the forefront in March 2023 when protesters supporting the movement removed an Indian flag from the country’s diplomatic mission in London, prompting stern condemnation from New Delhi and the summoning of the UK’s deputy high commissioner in India.

Two years later, in March 2025, a pro-Khalistan protester breached a police cordon during a visit by Indian Foreign Minister Subrahmanyam Jaishankar to London and tore an Indian flag.

Other disagreements have also tested bilateral relations.

India’s human rights record, including its treatment of religious minorities and policies in Indian-administered Kashmir, has drawn criticism from some British politicians and human rights organisations. New Delhi has rejected such criticism as interference in its internal affairs.

According to Cambridge’s Prabhu, these tensions between the countries often arise when “domestic political concerns meet the bilateral relationship”.

“Immigration and access for Indian students and professionals are sensitive issues, as are extradition cases and India’s concerns about potential anti-Indian activities in Britain,” he said.

“Such disagreements matter and should not be dismissed. But the relationship is sufficiently broad that friction in one area need not determine what happens in others.”

Despite the tensions, analysts say the two governments have developed sufficient shared interests to manage their disagreements.

Oxford’s de Estrada says both sides have demonstrated a willingness to “compartmentalise their differences in pursuit of shared economic and strategic interests”.

“While disagreements over Russia, Pakistan and occasionally the activities of Sikh separatist groups in Britain remain potential sources of friction, neither country appears willing to allow these issues to overshadow the broader relationship.”

Similarly, Cambridge professor Prabhu warned that while a serious security incident or sustained loss of trust could damage the relationship, both governments increasingly recognise the benefits of working together.

“Their expanding cooperation in trade, technology and security gives them strong reasons to manage their differences,” he said.

Moreover, Prabhu said Prince William and Catherine’s visit, with its emphasis on sustainability and innovation, reflects the changing nature of the relationship.

“I see Prince William’s visit in that light,” he said. “Its emphasis on sustainability and innovation symbolises a relationship that acknowledges its history but is increasingly concerned with what the two countries can build together.”

articles.title: What do Deutsche Bank leaks reveal about Trump, Epstein and Russia?
articles.summary: Deutsche Bank leaks expose ties to Trump, Epstein, and global elites amid scrutiny over past financial misconduct.
articles.body:
A leak of more than 15 million internal records from Deutsche Bank has shed new light on its dealings with United States President Donald Trump, the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein and other powerful figures.

The Inside Deutsche Bank investigation, published on Tuesday by a consortium of international news outlets, has put Germany’s biggest bank back in the spotlight after years of trying to rebuild its reputation following its failures to prevent money laundering.

Files containing millions of emails, minutes of meetings and internal reports were leaked by two whistleblowers whose identities and links to the institution have been withheld for their protection, according to Le Monde, one of the participating news outlets. The pair told the media groups they believed the bank was engaging in criminal activity and that releasing the documents was in the public interest.

Indian journalist Josy Joseph and South African journalist Khadija Sharife obtained the cache, which they then shared with more than 230 reporters from about 50 news organisations, including Der Spiegel, the Financial Times and The New York Times, in an internationally coordinated effort.

The material includes some nine million emails, as well as meeting minutes, due diligence reports and financial crime reports dating back to the early 2010s, many of them from the bank’s internal investigations.

The whistleblowers also passed the data to US prosecutors and financial crime authorities, and could be eligible for a reward if Washington prosecutes the bank based on their leaks. Le Monde said the whistleblowers were not paid by the journalists and placed no conditions on how the material was used.

Deutsche Bank said concerns raised by the investigation “date back many years” and that it had since strengthened its controls, adding that it did not expect any meaningful financial impact. The bank’s chairman reaffirmed the board’s support for chief executive Christian Sewing, who has run the institution since 2018.

“Deutsche Bank is a different bank today,” the bank said in a statement.

The files identify more than $3m in transactions involving Trump-owned companies, including payments linked to suspected Russian and Azerbaijani money-laundering networks.

Deutsche Bank extended loans to Trump for years, even after a string of bankruptcies and defaults at his businesses from the early 1990s. By January 2021, it was his biggest creditor, with about $340m in loans to his company outstanding.

That month, following the January 6 assault on the US Capitol by protesters wanting to stop the certification of Democrat Joe Biden’s win in the presidential election, the bank ceased doing business with him, according to The New York Times. Trump had claimed the election had been rigged against him, of which there has never been any proof.

The Financial Times reported that the bank inadvertently sent a Trump tax document to another client’s accountant in 2017, during his first term in office, and never told him about the error. Asked about the disclosure during his visit to Manila for the ASEAN summit on Tuesday, Trump said the bank should not have released that information.

“They shouldn’t have done it. It’s illegal for them to do it,” he said. Deutsche Bank declined to comment on his remarks.

The leaked records also reveal special monitoring that the bank applied to Trump’s accounts, and its handling of them has drawn scrutiny before.

In 2019, The New York Times reported that Deutsche Bank had failed to alert US authorities to suspicious transactions linked to Trump. The bank said at the time that none of its investigators had been prevented from escalating such concerns.

The leaked files list about $582m in transactions linked to Epstein, which were flagged internally as suspicious. That is more than double the amount previously identified as being overlooked or not reported by banks during US Senate investigations . When the Senate findings were released in August, a Deutsche Bank spokesperson said the bank regretted its “historical connection” with Epstein.

Epstein, who was a US financier, became a Deutsche Bank client in 2013, five years after pleading guilty in Florida to procuring a minor for prostitution, and remained a client until 2018. He died in a New York jail in 2019 while awaiting trial on sex trafficking charges.

Internal emails in the newly leaked cache indicate that senior executives approved Epstein as a client despite his conviction, and kept his accounts open even after warnings about the activities of Ghislaine Maxwell, his former girlfriend and associate. Maxwell was convicted in 2021 of helping Epstein sexually abuse teenage girls. She is currently serving a 20-year prison sentence.

The files also reveal information about payments linked to wealthy Epstein associates such as private equity billionaire Leon Black and Wall Street financier Glenn Dubin.

A review commissioned by Black’s firm previously found he had paid Epstein $158m between 2012 and 2017 for tax and estate planning advice. Black has sought to distance himself from Epstein, repeatedly denying wrongdoing or any knowledge of his abuse of girls and young women.

The leak comes years after the bank paid fines and settlements of more than $200m over its handling of Epstein-related finances. In 2020, regulators fined it $150m for compliance failures linked to Epstein and other high-risk clients, finding that he had held more than 40 accounts at the bank. In 2023, it agreed to pay $75m to settle a suit brought by women who alleged they had been abused by him.

The documents also detail Deutsche Bank’s business dealings in Russia up until Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, despite concerns raised by some managers.

They include previously undisclosed internal warnings about the bank’s continued dealings with wealthy Kremlin-connected clients despite sanctions and money laundering concerns.

Those named include Russian billionaires Roman Abramovich, the former owner of English football club Chelsea, and aluminium tycoon Oleg Deripaska. Both men were sanctioned by the United Kingdom in 2022. Suleiman Kerimov, another billionaire whose name appears in the files, was sanctioned by the US in 2014 and 2018.

Transactions associated with Rifaat al-Assad , the uncle of former Syrian President Bashar al-Assad, also appear in the files. Rifaat, who died in January, was convicted in France in 2020 of acquiring millions of euros’ worth of property with funds diverted from the Syrian state.

Other files concern figures connected to the Sarkozy-Libya affair, in which former French President Nicolas Sarkozy was convicted in 2025 of criminal conspiracy over efforts to secure funding for his 2007 campaign from the government of late Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi.

articles.title: In 1980, Billy Starr launched a Massachusetts charity bike ride; 46 years later, the Pan-Mass Challenge has donated more than $1.2 billion to cancer care, including a record $80 million presented on November 15
articles.summary: In 1980, Billy Starr launched a charity bike ride in Massachusetts with a simple idea: cyclists could turn miles into money for cancer research.
articles.body: In 1980, Billy Starr launched a charity bike ride in Massachusetts with a simple idea: cyclists could turn miles into money for cancer research. Forty six years later, the Pan-Mass Challenge has become one of the world’s most successful athletic fundraisers, donating more than $1.2 billion to Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, according to Dana-Farber and CBS Boston.On November 15, the organisation presented a record breaking $80 million gift to Dana-Farber at a celebratory brunch in Boston. The amount exceeded the 2026 fundraising goal by $1 million and represents the latest chapter in a fundraising effort that has grown from a single ride into a year round community of riders, volunteers, donors, and corporate partners.How the ride beganBilly Starr founded the Pan-Mass Challenge in 1980. The event began as a bike a thon designed to raise money for cancer care and research, and Starr remains its founder and chairman.The idea was straightforward. Riders would raise money through their participation, and the proceeds would support Dana-Farber’s work through the Jimmy Fund, the institute’s community fundraising arm.Over time, the event expanded beyond a single weekend ride. It became a broader fundraising platform that includes indoor cycling, gravel rides, and children’s events, all connected to the same mission.A record breaking giftThe $80 million gift presented on November 15 was the largest in the Pan-Mass Challenge’s history. It surpassed the 2026 goal of $79 million by $1 million, according to CBS Boston.The donation brings the PMC’s total contribution to Dana-Farber to more than $1.2 billion. That figure reflects decades of fundraising rather than a single year’s effort.Starr said the money represents more than a number. He described it as funding for the next clinical trial, the next breakthrough, the next life saved, and the next patient who gets to ring the bell at the end of treatment.Where the money goesFor the 20th consecutive year, 100 percent of every rider raised dollar goes directly to Dana-Farber. That model has helped the PMC become one of the most trusted names in athletic fundraising.The organisation says its support has helped drive recent breakthroughs at Dana-Farber, including the discovery of menin inhibitors, improvements in multi cancer early detection, and the development of new cell therapies such as CAR T and tumor infiltrating lymphocyte therapy.Dana-Farber president and CEO Benjamin Ebert, who is also a PMC rider, said the gift will help shape the future of cancer care and research at the institute. He described the donation as an important milestone and thanked the riders and volunteers who made it possible.More than a weekend rideThe Pan-Mass Challenge is no longer limited to its signature two day ride across Massachusetts. The organisation has expanded into other formats that allow more people to participate throughout the year.PMC Winter Cycle is an indoor spin event held at Fenway Park. PMC Unpaved is a gravel bike ride, while PMC Kids Rides are mini bike a thons for children ages 2 to 15.These additional events help broaden the organisation’s reach. They bring in riders who may not be able to complete the main ride, while still contributing to the same fundraising goal.A community built around a causeThe Pan-Mass Challenge attracts riders and volunteers from 44 states and eight countries. It also draws support from more than 300,000 individual donors, according to Dana-Farber.The organisation says its success comes from combining the efforts of cyclists, volunteers, corporate sponsors, and individual donors. The goal is to maximise fundraising efficiency while increasing the annual gift.Starr said he has never been prouder of the PMC community. He argued that riders, volunteers, donors, and corporate partners understood what was at stake and helped push the organisation past its goal.Why the milestone mattersThe $80 million gift arrives at a time when federal research support and grant approval rates are shrinking, while cancer rates continue to climb. Dana-Farber says more than 20 million new cancer cases are projected worldwide in 2026 alone.In that context, the PMC’s sustained giving has become an important force for keeping research moving forward. The organisation’s support helps fund studies, clinical trials, and treatments that may not otherwise move as quickly.For the riders and volunteers who make the event possible, the milestone is a reminder that their work has real world impact. articles.title: Brain cancer patients at UHCW demand public inquiry into chemotherapy scandal
articles.summary: A wider review of affected patients should be discussed with the government, the report recommends.
articles.body:
Brain cancer patients who were given years of unnecessary chemotherapy are calling for a public inquiry, after a review found people were severely harmed under an NHS trust's care.

Some were misdiagnosed while others were told if they stopped temozolomide (TMZ) treatment they would die, despite this not being true.

The Royal College of Physicians (RCP) investigated 20 cases at University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust.

The drug is typically meant to be taken for six months but in one case a patient of Prof Ian Brown was given more than 100 cycles of chemotherapy over a period of 13 years. They later developed leukaemia as a side-effect of too much chemotherapy.

Becky Jones, who had 11 years of the treatment for a cancer she did not have, has told the BBC she was "absolutely disgusted" that "chemotherapy was dished out like it was sweets".

"I have two young children and to think once upon a time I might not have been there for their future kills me every day and it's all down to one person," the 35-year-old added.

She is one of more than 40 patients taking legal action against the NHS Trust. The mum-of-two was 21 when she was told she had a grade 4 glioblastoma and six to 12 months to live.

After more than 100 cycles of chemotherapy it was found she had never had a brain tumour and that her imaging was consistent with tumefactive demyelination, a less serious lesion.

She said of the report: "The findings are worse than I ever expected them to be.

"A national inquiry needs to happen and things need to be tightened up so it can't happen to anyone else.

"I don't think I'll ever find closure until the trust accept what they have done wrong and are held accountable. I would like answers."

The review, released on Wednesday, was commissioned by the trust following the retirement of one of its doctors.

Brown, referred to as Dr Y in the RCP's report, did not take part in the review and refused to comment when approached by the BBC at his home.

University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire (UHCW) NHS Trust has apologised for "failures" within its neuro-oncology service under the care of the retired clinical oncologist.

Chief executive Professor Andy Hardy and trust chair Sue Noyes said in a statement: "This is far below the standards our patients deserve and that we expect. We let you down, and for that we offer our sincere apologies."

Brown was employed there from 1996 to 2024 and concerns over his practice were raised by colleagues when his patients were handed over upon his retirement in December 2023.

Medics found people on long-term repeated cycles of TMZ, against standard practice and national guidelines.

Some patients had also been left on treatment despite their cancer progressing, when moving to the best supportive care for their symptoms would have been a better choice.

TMZ, a chemotherapy drug that is sometimes used for glioblastoma and astrocytoma brain tumours, should usually be taken post radiotherapy for six cycles, usually over six months, but some patients have told the BBC they received it for many years.

The review warned there may be many more affected patients, with 83 receiving extended TMZ treatment between 2017 and 2023.

Overall, the RCP examined 20 cases of care under Brown, though the number of patients affected is higher - including those who have since died.

Working to strict definitions of harm, the review team concluded six patients had suffered severe harm, five moderate harm and eight low levels of harm. In the final case, the review team could not reach a judgement on moderate or severe harm.

Among other recommendations, the RCP said that any wider review of patients who received the treatment and have since died should be discussed with the Department of Health and Social Care.

"There is a large cohort of deceased patients who have received this non-standard chemotherapy regime, who may potentially have come to harm," the report said.

"To review every patient would be a significant and costly undertaking. The Trust should determine whether such a step is appropriate, and if so, discuss with the DHSC and/or NHS England how such a review would proceed."

Father-of-three Mark Poulton, from Redditch, Worcestershire, said he had been left in "constant pain" with spells of depression after undergoing chemotherapy for a decade, only to discover two years ago that he had been misdiagnosed.

The 54-year-old told the BBC: "I feel angry that I've gone through 10 years of TMZ that I probably shouldn't have done and the report backs that.

"You get a cancer diagnosis of any sort and you feel you will collapse, then you go to a hospital and you're in the right place, you feel safe, only to find out 10 to 12 years later that you were abused by the system that failed me and the other patients involved.

"More needs to be done, it can't end here with this review. We need action so it doesn't happen again."

In 2014 he was told he had oligodendroglioma, an aggressive brain tumour, but found out in 2024 that he actually had astrocytoma, a different type of cancer.

The review also highlighted patients who were exposed to a "significant lifetime risk" of developing secondary cancers and other health problems after several years of non-standard chemotherapy.

One, who received the drug for 10 years, experienced "significant toxicity", including ongoing fatigue, nausea and a "severe episode" of ophthalmic shingles and galactorrhoea caused by a drug prescribed to treat chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting.

The review also referred to a Mr N, who the BBC understands to be clinical nurse specialist Ian Edwards.

Some patients were advised implicitly and explicitly that stopping treatment would be harmful, the review said.

There was also evidence in some cases of patients being given misleading information.

The review team heard in interviews that a small number of patients had requested discontinuation of their treatment, which Edwards then discussed with Brown and acted upon, however no evidence of this was seen in the cases reviewed.

"In one case when the patient questioned their treatment, they were told by Mr N (Edwards) that Dr Y (Brown) was 'legally bound' to continue it," they added.

Edwards has also since retired from the trust, UHCW confirmed, adding it had made a formal regulatory referral to the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) regulator.

Legal firm Brabners, which represents more than 40 patients and is calling for an independent public inquiry , said cases had been referred to the police but no action had yet been taken.

Becky Addison, from the firm, said: "Now is the opportunity that everyone needs to sit up and look at how important this is for patients that they get the answers that they deserve.

"They've had their lives taken away from them in unimaginable ways and all that they need at the moment is answers, transparency and accountability and that will come by way of a statutory public inquiry."

All living patients receiving TMZ at the trust have already had their care reviewed again internally to ensure it aligned with expected standards, the UHCW trust has said.

A "comprehensive independent external clinical review process" will also evaluate all living patients who received over 12 cycles of TMZ under Brown.

The trust added: "We have initiated discussions with the NHS England regional director of patient safety to establish clear requirements and methodology for reviewing the cohort of deceased patients who received non-standard chemotherapy regime."

articles.title: Traumas of Sudan war lead to wave of drug addiction
articles.summary: Anguish caused by conflict sees a growing number of young people turn to drugs.
articles.body:
Khartoum, Sudan – Mohammed Awad never imagined that his life would change so dramatically when war broke out in his home city of Khartoum in April 2023 when he was aged 17.

He found himself displaced and forced out of school, moving from one state to another accompanied by his cousins and searching for a safe place where he could escape the horrors of war.

But what began as a journey in search of safety became the beginning of a personal tragedy, one experienced by millions of people in Sudan who are in the midst of one of the world’s worst humanitarian crises in which killing and displacement have become routine.

“I started taking drugs to forget what I have seen and the horrors I have been through in Khartoum during the first months of the war. My friends and my cousin were killed in front of me,” he told Al Jazeera. “I am trying to recover now, so I can proceed with my education and life.”

The conflict between the Sudanese armed forces (SAF) and Rapid Support Forces (RSF) paramilitary group saw the capital become one of the initial epicentres of this power struggle between the two former military allies.

The war trapped thousands of people in Khartoum State in their homes for weeks or forced them to flee, but since the SAF expelled the RSF from the region in May last year, it has now become a haven for millions of people fleeing fighting elsewhere in Sudan. The war has led to a humanitarian catastrophe with at least 59,000 people killed and 14 million people forced to leave their homes in a country with a population of 52 million. Displacement is more than the simple act of moving from one place to another but a journey marked by fear, anxiety and instability with increasingly limited options in life.

For those such as Awad caught in the pressures of displacement and the absence of a supportive environment, drugs have become a way of dealing with an unbearable reality.

“I entered rehabilitation centres many times, and I quickly returned to addiction. I take pills and sometimes weed. I want to stop, but I keep failing over and over again,” Awad said.

The war in Sudan has not only severely impacted individual civilians’ lives but has also torn apart the social fabric of the country. The lack of security and poverty have also led to a proliferation of drugs manufacturing and trade, particularly the highly addictive amphetamine Captagon. According to government officials, areas currently or formerly under RSF control are a particular problem.

The Qadreen Center for Addiction Treatment is one of the few charitable institutions dealing with the problem in Khartoum, and doctors in the capital told Al Jazeera there is growing demand for their services.

“The centre continues to provide its medical services both before and after the outbreak of the war,” the centre’s director, Lubna Ali, said.

“Following the war, it witnessed a significant increase in the number of cases seeking treatment amid growing needs for mental health and addiction recovery services.”

Since the war has broken out, the centre has treated 10,100 cases ranging from patients in need of psychological support for war-related trauma to those with drug addiction. Ali said 135 such individuals have been treated “in their recovery journey”.

Young people are particularly affected by the war, witnessing horrific violence, displacement, the loss of friends and relatives, interrupted education and quickly declining employment opportunities.

Weakened institutions and a deteriorating security situation have undermined oversight efforts and the ability of health services to respond to the addiction crisis.

Dr Aisha Almobasher, a psychiatrist at the Bitmakaly National Organization, which provides psychological and therapeutic support to individuals affected by war and addiction, told Al Jazeera that some areas of Sudan are worse affected by the drug problem than others.

“The growing number of people seeking treatment suggests that this is more than a passing phenomenon. Many of those struggling with addiction come from areas previously controlled by the Rapid Support Forces, RSF, where, following their withdrawal, drugs reportedly became more widely available and trafficking networks expanded,” she told Al Jazeera.

“In some states, drugs also became a means of attracting and recruiting young people, particularly into the ranks of RSF fighters, drawing many of them onto a dark path.”

According to a report published by the Sudan Transparency and Policy Tracker in March, 19 incidents involving the seizures of drugs or manufacturing facilities were recorded in Sudan from 2015 to 2025 with a notable acceleration since the outbreak of the war.

These figures refer to seizures and estimated production capacity not actual drug consumption. Nevertheless, they reveal the scale of the problem and the transformation taking place in the country’s illicit drug trade.

Major-General (Legal) Mohamed Al-Moatasim Okasha, director of Sudan’s General Directorate for Anti-Narcotics, said its teams have dealt with an increase in drug manufacturing and production since the war began.

They have found advanced drug production facilities in areas retaken from the RSF by the SAF, including areas in and around Khartoum. El-Radom, an area in South Darfur State in western Sudan, has become a well-known cannabis-growing region, he said.

“It remains under RSF control and is expected to return to the control of the Sudanese armed forces soon. Throughout the past three years of war, antinarcotics operations in this area have been suspended with no other authority able to effectively address the problem due to its inaccessibility under RSF control,” he told Al Jazeera.

“Meanwhile, the use and circulation of other narcotic substances have been increasing, particularly Captagon, crystal methamphetamine (ice) and drugs such as tramadol. However, these substances remain less widespread than cannabis and other traditionally prevalent drugs.”

A huge facility for manufacturing Captagon pills was recently discovered by the SAF north of Khartoum, close to an oil refinery that was formerly under RSF control.

SAF forces uncovered drugs manufacturing equipment valued at about $3m. The facility was capable of producing 100,000 Captagon pills per hour with raw materials potentially able to produce 700 million pills.

“These are not merely allegations of drug trafficking, smuggling or distribution. They are evidence of industrial-scale drug production taking place in areas that were under RSF control,” Okasha told Al Jazeera.

“As for drug use among combatants, there have been reports and testimonies indicating that quantities of narcotic substances were found in the possession of captured militia members. This highlights how widespread these substances have become and how readily accessible they are to fighters.”

Drug trafficking and manufacturing have become weapons of war, not just illicit sources of income, and they are directly impacting the conflict between the SAF and RSF, he said. Captagon has become a regional issue with facilities producing the drug in Syria during the rule of former President Bashar al-Assad flooding the illicit market.

While the new government in Damascus is trying to crack down on these facilities in southern Syria, Captagon production is a growing problem in other regional conflict areas such as Sudan.

“Sudan faces this growing threat amid the ongoing conflict,” Okasha said. “Through strong nationwide coordination, we are intensifying seizures and disrupting smuggling, trafficking and production networks. Our mission is to stop the spread of narcotics, protect our youth and safeguard future generations. Combating drugs is a national security priority.”

“The drug problem in Sudan cannot be viewed in isolation. It is a regional challenge, and Sudan is part of a region experiencing a growing drug crisis.”
